name: UNICEF USA
mission: Over eight decades, the United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) has built an unprecedented global support system for the world's children. UNICEF relentlessly works day in and day out to deliver the essentials that give every child an equitable chance in life: health care and immunizations, safe water and sanitation, nutrition, education, emergency relief and more. UNICEF USA advances the global mission of UNICEF by rallying the American public to support the world's most vulnerable children. Together, we have helped save more children's lives than any other humanitarian organization.
theoryOfChange: UNICEF USA, through its Impact Fund for Children, has co-developed and published a "Child-Lens Investing Framework." This framework serves as a central guiding document for investors, asset owners, regulators, and other stakeholders to frame investment strategies and direct capital toward advancing positive child outcomes and minimizing child harm. The framework includes core principles, a case for investment, an analysis of the global market landscape, and a description of the Child-Lens Investment ecosystem. Additionally, UNICEF USA's Impact Fund reports impact through an "Input/Output/Outcomes Framework," which provides the number and category of beneficiaries, quantitative program outputs, and targeted long-term outcomes for each acceleration to UNICEF. The UNICEF USA Child Friendly Cities Initiative (CFCI) also provides a "child rights framework" for building child-friendly cities and communities, which includes a "Framework for Action" outlining goals, results, and strategies.

In FY2025, the organization reported <cite id="1">Total Revenue of $835,217,861</cite>. Its work spans clean water, emergency nutrition, and education across major global regions [9]. On financial efficiency, the organization operates with a <cite id="1">Program expense ratio of 83.1%</cite>. This ratio beats the <cite id="1">75% industry standard</cite> for non-profit program spending, though it is slightly under the <cite id="1">peer median of 83.3%</cite>. Additionally, the organization maintains high fundraising efficiency, spending <cite id="1">$0.10 per $1 raised</cite> in donations. Revenue declined 13% in the most recent fiscal year, moving from $829,050,932 in FY2023 to $720,404,955 in FY2024. Operating reserves remain lean, providing <cite id="1">2.8 months of working capital</cite>.
